_doc: THE MATTER LIBRARY — the data spine of the Substrate Engine.
Commissioned 2026-07-18, the human, verbatim: 'a library of materials .... esentaly
typs of mater ind its propertys of interaction and also what the surface looks like
even know it is not a surface but more of an average!'
THREE COLUMNS, exactly as commissioned: (1) types of matter, (2) properties of
INTERACTION (pairwise, via interface FAMILIES so N materials never becomes an N^2
hand-written matrix — only exceptional pairs get explicit entries), (3) appearance
as a DISTRIBUTION, never a painted surface: every appearance value is a mean plus a
spread, because a real surface IS the statistical average of its microstructure
(roughness literally = variance of micro-facet normals). The splat emitter SAMPLES
the distribution per particle; a coalesced aggregate uses the MEAN — coalesce is
taking the average at a coarser scale, fracture is sampling individuals back out.
EVERY NUMBER CARRIES PROVENANCE (same taxonomy as Malcolm's envelope walls).
No number without a tag. 'provisional' numbers are DEBTS — tb-0172 upgrades them
to researched with cached sources, or corrects them.
CONSUMERS (one library, four readers): core/matter.py adhesion (physical +
interaction), core/splat_emit.py optics (appearance; wiring task tb-0174),
rung D-prime's UE Substrate slab materials (appearance), core/trainables/*
(physical + interaction columns as seed values; 'trained' provenance flows back).

provenance_classes.seed: verbatim from CHIMERA_VISION.py (the game's own tables — SURFACE_TABLE etc.)
provenance_classes.code: verbatim from proven studio code (e.g. splat_emit.py OPTICAL, matter.py adhesion) — survived a witnessed render/run
provenance_classes.researched: cited external measurement with a cached source on disk
provenance_classes.provisional: model-knowledge estimate, plausible but UNVERIFIED — a debt owed to tb-0172
provenance_classes.trained: output of a trainer objective (docs/objectives/<f>.trained.json) — cite the objective
provenance_classes.design: a chosen game value with no real-world referent, named as such

families._doc: Interface families keep interactions O(families^2), not O(materials^2). Pair rules below are family x family; materials inherit them; 'pair_exceptions' overrides for specific couples.

family_pair_rules._doc: Qualitative interaction classes + friction multiplier (applied to the softer party's traction). Sparse: unlisted pairs default to {contact:'dry', friction_mult:1.0, adhesion:'none', thermal:'slow'}.

mineral_dry|metallic.note: regolith dust electrostatically coats metal — why METAL makes_print=true in the seed despite being hard

organic_wet|organic_wet.note: matter.py: like-tissue cohesion drives the radial sort

organic_wet|organic_hard.note: muscle-bone junction REQUIRES the typed tendon connector (matter.py rung 1.5: adhesion alone cannot hold the interface)

density_kg_m3.note: Lunar Sourcebook ch.9 / Carrier et al. 1991: in-situ ~1.30-1.92 g/cc; mean=1500 matches commonly cited ~1.5 g/cc typical value (Wikipedia 'Lunar soil'). Spread widened to cover full cited near-surface range.

friction_angle_deg.note: Mitchell et al. 1972 (3rd Lunar Sci. Conf.): friction angle 30-50 deg for lunar soil; mean=35 is lower-middle of band appropriate for loose surface material (stiffness_class: loose_granular).

cohesion_kpa.note: Mitchell et al. 1972: cohesion most-probable range 0.1-1.0 kN/m2 (kPa); mean=0.5 centers the cited range.

grain_size_mm.note: Carrier 2003: D50 ~72 micron across ~350 samples from 7 landing sites; NTRS 20210026714: individual samples 24.5-118.5 micron. Mean=0.072mm matches D50 exactly.

appearance.note: grey-tan regolith; calibrate against the NASA reference canon (tb-0172) and the live level's M_Sand

density_kg_m3.note: Adjacent citation only: Carrier et al. 1991 gives 1.30 g/cc as loosest measured ordinary regolith; basin is explicitly fluffier/looser than that. No direct measurement exists — extrapolating below the cited floor without a measurement would be fabrication.

friction_angle_deg.note: Mitchell et al. 1972: same 30-50 deg band as sand; basin's very_loose_granular tag places it even lower in the cited band.

cohesion_kpa.note: Mitchell et al. 1972: cohesion range 0.1-1.0 kPa; mean=0.2 sits at the low end consistent with basin's looser design intent.

grain_size_mm.note: NTRS 20210026714 (sample 10084): mature mare regolith D50 ~24.5 micron; basin modeled as fine dust-pond analog of the finest measured sample.

appearance.note: finer + slightly paler than sand (dust pond)

density_kg_m3.note: Geology/engineering references: basalt density range 2700-3300 kg/m3, average ~2900 kg/m3.

youngs_modulus_gpa.note: Quaglio et al. 2020 (Advances in Materials Science and Engineering): intact basalt at ambient temp, Young's modulus ≈ 78 ± 19 GPa.

grain_size_mm.note: surface texture scale, not mineral grains

appearance.note: dark basalt; high mottle variance is what reads as rock vs the smoother regolith

density_kg_m3.note: NIST / engineering references: Al 6061-T6 density = 2700 kg/m3 (temper-independent).

youngs_modulus_gpa.note: NIST / engineering references: Al 6061-T6 Young's modulus = 69 GPa (68.9-70 GPa across sources, temper-independent). Spread tightened to reflect well-established constant.

makes_print.note: dust film on the plating takes prints; storm-proof (seed keeps METAL prints through storms)

appearance.note: brushed alloy; roughness_var carries the wear-streak variation

density_kg_m3.note: Wikipedia 'Ice' / standard physics: density of ice = 0.9167-0.9168 g/cm3 at 0°C = 917 kg/m3 (extremely well-known constant). Spread tightened.

youngs_modulus_gpa.note: Ice-mechanics literature: polycrystalline ice E ≈ 9.0-9.3 GPa near 0°C (e.g. ScienceDirect atmospheric icing study). Spread widened to reflect literature scatter.

appearance.note: the one environment material with real subsurface depth — the slab's MFP field earns its keep here

density_kg_m3.note: habitat floor composite — a built thing, no natural referent

appearance.note: clean matte panel; the LOW variance is the point — built things are uniform, grown/natural things are not. Uniformity IS the tell.

density_kg_m3.note: ICRP Publication 110: soft tissue density tables.

tear_threshold_class.note: THE_MATTER_MODEL SS9: the wound reveals structure

appearance.note: means verbatim from splat_emit.py OPTICAL — survived rung A's witnessed relight renders (tb-0168). mfp_mm provisional (skin dermis ~1-3mm, graphics BSSRDF literature — verify via tb-0172).

density_kg_m3.note: ICRP + Ward et al. 2005: skeletal muscle density.

stiffness_class.note: behavior=contract is the ONE behavior field the game reads (THE_MATTER_MODEL SS2)

anisotropy.note: muscle is directional — the appearance AND the mechanics share the fiber axis

appearance.note: means verbatim from splat_emit.py OPTICAL (tb-0168 witnessed). Striation = anisotropic roughness along the fiber axis, not a texture.

density_kg_m3.note: Biomechanics reviews: cortical bone 'assumed apparent density of 1800 kg/m3' — typical value used in biomechanical analyses; spread widened to cover 1800-2000 kg/m3 variation band.

youngs_modulus_gpa.note: Biomechanics reviews: cortical bone modulus 16-22 GPa (lumbar spine region); direct microspecimen measurements 20.7 GPa (ultrasonic) / 18.6 GPa (mechanical). Mean=18 centers the band; spread widened to reflect wider clinical range.

pair_exceptions._doc: Explicit couples that override family rules. boot|X rows ARE the seed's SURFACE_TABLE read as what it always was: the player-contact interaction row.

muscle|bone.note: matter.py rung 1.5: the typed tendon held 81% bonded, 0.00 skin/air exposure where the control drifted — adhesion alone cannot hold this interface

skin|muscle.note: matter.py radial sort: skin shells muscle unattended when adhesion profiles differ

storm_wind|sand.note: UWeatherSubsystem: storm end filters footprints to METAL only — the memento mori. Cadence now TRAINED: docs/objectives/weather.trained.json
